summary: AI observability has become essential in 2026 as LLM systems move into production, enabling teams to trace failures, monitor costs, debug prompts, and continuously improve model performance. Without proper monitoring, teams operate blind to token waste, latency spikes, and quality regressions that directly impact both user experience and infrastructure spend. DevOps-style observability tooling is now a standard expectation for any serious LLM deployment, with adoption accelerating across startups and enterprises alike.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, agent runs, chain execution, prompt performance, evaluation results, and human-in-the-loop feedback for LangChain and LangGraph applications
features: Native LangChain and LangGraph integration with zero-config tracing
Best-in-class trace UI for graph-structured agent workflows
Human-in-the-loop evaluation workflows and annotation tools
Prompt variant comparison and versioning
Dataset management for regression testing
Online and offline evaluation pipelines
Team collaboration and debugging tools
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39/seat/month; overage ~$2.50 per 1,000 traces at standard retention. Approximately £80/month for typical team usage.
tools.best_for: Teams already using LangChain or LangGraph who need deep agent observability and structured evaluation workflows in production

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, token usage, cost per request, latency, model performance, and user sessions via a proxy gateway layer
features: Proxy-based setup requiring minimal code changes (2-minute integration)
Per-request and per-session cost tracking and visualization
Prompt template management and versioning
User-level usage analytics and segmentation
Rate limiting and caching to reduce API spend
Open-source and self-hostable
SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA compliance on Team tier
tools.pricing: Free Hobby tier at 10K requests/month; Pro at $79/month (unlimited seats, usage-based beyond included volume); Team at $799/month (compliance features); custom Enterprise pricing with SAML SSO and on-prem options. Approximately £20/month for 100K requests on standard plans.
tools.best_for: Teams prioritizing simplicity, fast setup, and cost visibility who want the cheapest managed option with strong cost tracking without complex configuration

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: ML experiments, LLM prompt traces, model training runs, evaluation metrics, dataset versions, and artifact lineage across the full ML lifecycle
features: Experiment tracking and hyperparameter logging
LLM prompt and completion tracing via W&B Weave
Model evaluation dashboards and metric comparison
Dataset and artifact versioning
Collaborative reporting and visualization
Integration with major ML frameworks and LLM providers
Support for fine-tuning and RLHF workflows
tools.pricing: Free tier for individuals with limited usage; Teams plan at $50/user/month; Enterprise pricing available on request. Storage and compute costs vary by usage.
tools.best_for: ML and research teams managing both traditional model training and LLM experimentation who need unified experiment tracking alongside production observability

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: LLM traces, embeddings, model performance, data drift, hallucination rates, prompt quality, and enterprise-scale telemetry across deployed AI systems
features: Arize Phoenix open-source tracing with OpenTelemetry support
Embedding visualization and drift detection
LLM evaluation with built-in and custom metrics
Real-time alerting on performance degradation
Support for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline monitoring
Enterprise-grade telemetry and compliance features
Integration with major LLM providers and orchestration frameworks
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host (source-available license); Arize AI cloud platform offers a free tier with limited volume; enterprise pricing available on request and scales with data volume and seats.
tools.best_for: Enterprise teams needing robust production telemetry, embedding-level debugging, RAG pipeline observability, and compliance-grade monitoring at scale

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt versions, token usage, cost, latency, evaluation scores, and user feedback across multi-step LLM pipelines
features: Open-source with full self-hosting capability
Detailed trace and span visualization for complex pipelines
Prompt management with versioning and A/B comparison
Built-in and custom evaluation scoring
Dataset creation from production traces for offline evaluation
SDKs for Python, JS/TS, and OpenAI-compatible APIs
Native integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and more
tools.pricing: Cloud free tier for under 50K events/month; paid cloud at approximately £20 for 500K events/month; self-hosted version free with ~£30/month infrastructure cost and approximately 2 hours/month maintenance. One of the most cost-effective options available.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting open-source flexibility, strong prompt management, and cost-effective cloud or self-hosted tracing without vendor lock-in

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM API calls, token counts, latency, model inputs and outputs, and span-level trace data via OpenTelemetry-compatible instrumentation
features: OpenTelemetry-native instrumentation for LLM calls
Auto-instrumentation for OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and other providers
Vendor-agnostic: sends data to any OTLP-compatible backend
Lightweight SDK with minimal code changes required
Span-level visibility into prompts, completions, and token usage
Open-source under permissive license
Works alongside existing observability stacks
tools.pricing: Fully open-source and free to use. Backend storage and infrastructure costs depend on chosen observability platform (e.g., OpenObserve, Grafana, Datadog).
tools.best_for: Engineering teams with existing OpenTelemetry infrastructure who want standards-based LLM instrumentation that integrates into their current observability stack without adopting a new platform

tools.name: OpenObserve
tools.monitors: LLM traces, per-model and per-session costs, infrastructure metrics, logs, application performance, and frontend (RUM) monitoring in a unified platform
features: Native OpenTelemetry LLM tracing support
Per-model and per-session cost tracking
Unified infrastructure and LLM observability in a single deployment
Logs, metrics, traces, and real-user monitoring (RUM) combined
Open-source and self-hostable
Eliminates need for separate DevOps and LLM monitoring stacks
Comprehensive comparison capabilities across open-source tools
tools.pricing: Open-source and free to self-host; cloud pricing available with a free tier. Infrastructure costs vary by deployment scale.
tools.best_for: Teams tired of managing separate DevOps telemetry and LLM observability stacks who want a single unified platform covering infrastructure, logs, metrics, and LLM tracing together

tools.name: Confident AI (DeepEval)
tools.monitors: LLM output quality, hallucination rates, relevance, toxicity, and 50+ evaluation metrics across model responses in both offline and online evaluation modes
features: 50+ open-sourced evaluation metrics via DeepEval framework
Used by teams at OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft
Automated regression testing for LLM outputs
Custom metric creation for domain-specific evaluation
Online monitoring with real-time quality scoring
Dataset management and benchmark comparisons
CI/CD pipeline integration for continuous evaluation
tools.pricing: DeepEval open-source framework is free; Confident AI cloud platform pricing available on request with usage-based tiers.
tools.best_for: Teams prioritizing LLM output quality assurance and evaluation depth over infrastructure monitoring, especially those needing rigorous automated testing pipelines

cost_tips: Implement prompt caching and request deduplication: tools like Helicone offer built-in caching that can serve repeated or near-identical requests from cache rather than making a new API call, reducing token spend by 20-40% for applications with repetitive queries or shared context windows.

Right-size your model selection per task: use observability data to identify which requests actually require frontier models like GPT-4o or Claude Opus versus cheaper models like GPT-4o-mini or Haiku. Routing simple classification, summarization, or retrieval tasks to smaller models can cut per-request costs by 10-20x without measurable quality loss.

Monitor and trim token bloat in system prompts and context: use tracing tools like Langfuse or LangSmith to audit token counts per span and identify unnecessarily verbose system prompts, redundant context injection, or RAG chunks that exceed what the model actually uses. Reducing average prompt length by 20% directly reduces costs by the same proportion.

Set up cost alerts and per-user or per-session budgets: tools like Helicone and LangSmith allow you to configure spending thresholds and rate limits at the user, session, or application level, preventing runaway costs from prompt injection attacks, infinite agent loops, or unexpected traffic spikes before they appear on your monthly bill.
